messages.subject: Moderated mediation with longitudinal data
parts:
Hi,

I am new user in Lavaan. I want to see the effect of X(which is exogenous and time invariant) on Y(measured in 10 time waves) through mediating effect of M. This relationship of M to Y is moderated by V. All these variables are latent and measured by proxies.What would be the code to do it in lavaan?
Thanks in advance.

Best
Ahsan

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation with longitudinal data
parts: I want to see the effect of X(which is exogenous and time invariant) on Y(measured in 10 time waves) through mediating effect of M.

How?  Are you going to measure 10 effects of X (one on each of 10 times), or an effect of X on latent growth parameters or difference scores, or will X be concurrent with time 1 in an autoregressive panel model for Y?  Lots of options, but whatever your theoretical model is, you can specify regression parameters in the model syntax using the ~ operator:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax1.html
This relationship of M to Y is moderated by V. All these variables are latent and measured by proxies.

That could be a problem.  Interaction terms among observed variables can be included by adding their product terms to the model syntax.  But latent variables are not observed, so their products cannot be calculated.  You could use LMS estimation in Mplus or the R package nlsem, but in lavaan you could only use product indicators of constructs that represent latent interaction, as described in the References on the ?indProd help page of the semTools package.  But the centering procedures necessary to use product indicators would make all means zero, which would prevent estimation of change over time (e.g., in a latent growth curve model).
What would be the code to do it in lavaan?

Jason Newsom's longitudinal SEM book has accompanying Mplus and lavaan syntax.  See example 7.5 for exogenous predictors of growth factors, and example 7.6 if your growth factors have multiple-indicator common factors as their indicators.

http://www.longitudinalsem.com/
